newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sampo wants Merita decision on its stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sampo wants Merita decision on its stake - paper.

text.p: Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Sampo wants its largest owner, banking group Merita Oy to make a decision on what it aims to do with its ownership, business daily Kauppalehti quoted Sampo CEO Jouko Leskinen as saying.
In a first page summary of an interview with Leskinen in Kauppalehti's weekly supplement Optio, the paper said Leskinen wanted a clear signal to the stock market.
"The best of all would be a final decision. In other words, that Merita would make a decision one way or the other and say what this is that they have decided," it quoted Leskinen as saying.
Merita owns 18 percent of Sampo's share capital and also has a 10 percent stake in Sampo's second largest owner Unsa Oy, which holds 14 percent, a Sampo spokesman said.
Sampo owns 1.47 percent of Merita's share capital.
Merita also owns 16 percent of shares in Sampo's biggest rival Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola.

"If Merita were to publicly announce that its investments in Sampo and Pohjola are good and that nothing but financial investment are linked to them, the situation would calm," Leskinen was quoted in the article in Optio, delayed in publication due to printing problems.
"Now there is speculation that this ownership would lead to a structural change although it does not have to lead to anything," he added.
Leskinen was also quoted as saying that Sampo did not aim to make a technical profit on insurance operations alone.
"Among our clients there would be a terrible row if we could show a positive result on the technical account in insurance. Then we would have mispriced our policies at the end of 1995," he said.
Insurers' results should be read at the bottom line, after investment earnings, he said.
